body.statement: Fix an integer \(b\geq2\) and an activity \(0<\lambda<b^b/(b-1)^{b+1}\).  For \(Z_G(\lambda)=\sum_{I\in\mathcal I(G)}\lambda^{|I|}\), there is a deterministic fully polynomial-time approximation scheme on finite graphs \(G\) of maximum degree at most \(b+1\): on input \(G\) and \(0<\eta<1\), it returns bounds \(Z_1\leq Z_G(\lambda)\leq Z_2\leq(1+\eta)Z_1\) in time polynomial in \(|V|\) and \(\eta^{-1}\), with the polynomial exponent allowed to depend on the fixed \(b\) and \(\lambda\).

source.verbatim_statement: Corollary 2.8 There exists a deterministic algorithm such that for every positive integer \(b\) and any \(\lambda<\lambda_c(b)\), on input of any graph \(G\) of maximum degree \(b+1\), the algorithm approximates the partition function \(Z_G^\lambda\) to within a factor \((1+\epsilon)\) in time polynomial in \((1+\epsilon)n/\epsilon\), where the exponent depends on \(b\) and \(\lambda\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Corollary 2.8 of Dror Weitz's author-hosted March 16, 2006 manuscript, matching the STOC 2006 paper; the immediately preceding definitions identify \(Z_G^\lambda=\sum_I\lambda^{|I|}\), and the corollary states the deterministic approximation guarantee used here.
